items.explanation: Cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72." Both 12-lead ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at about 139-144 bpm with no discernible P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The note and the same-day ECGs conflict.

Patient takes escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list; current order 438668cc of 2026-07-18). His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08 - the tracing that was reviewed when escitalopram was started) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 484 ms and Bazett QTc 516 ms, i.e. >= 500 ms, despite the 2024-05-14 note describing the QT as acceptable. Prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-03-18).

Patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list, maximum recommended dose exceeded for many patients; current order 62da0901 of 2026-07-15). Her most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 480 ms and Bazett QTc 519 ms, i.e. >= 500 ms, requiring prescriber review. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal.

Amiodarone (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10. The 9/1/2025 memo applies (start before 3/1/2026), so an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. A 12-lead ECG (106885519) was obtained on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (The result itself is abnormal - QTc 539 ms - and is flagged separately.)

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07 (5 days), so the requirement was completed; it showed sinus rhythm with QTc 378 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-02-12, before the 3/1/2026 revision, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (due 2026-03-14). ECG 101538691 was obtained on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was completed; it showed sinus rhythm with QTc 378 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10. The start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was not recorded until 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days (by 2026-08-15) under the revised memo. The only ECG in the chart is from 2025-12-25, before the medication was started, and no ECG has been obtained since. The requirement is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so an ECG was due within 14 days (by 2026-08-24). The telephone note of 2026-08-25 (5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15, so under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been recorded since the start (last tracing 2025-03-09), but the due date is after the 2026-09-24 review date, so the requirement is not yet due.

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler documents a warfarin dose increase from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily for a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, within the window, so the requirement was met.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-06-22) document persistent atrial fibrillation; she was also on a DOAC during a Jan-2025 admission (apixaban order a104f805). Current outpatient medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only - no oral anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age 80, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction with residual deficits, old myocardial infarction/coronary atherosclerosis, female). Guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is indicated; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD documents a warfarin dose decrease from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the anticoagulation protocol for a home INR of 3.4 (a dose change a clinic pharmacist is permitted to make). The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since 2026-06-17, so the follow-up INR is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (Condition 7010d0e5) carried in every cardiology clinic note. Current medications at the last visit (2026-06-27) are levothyroxine only - no anticoagulant and no record of one being stopped for a documented reason. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition 66dd1300) and prior embolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis. Current medications at the last clinic visit (2026-06-23) are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate - no anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke, female). Anticoagulation is strongly indicated for secondary stroke prevention.

48-year-old man with atrial fibrillation/paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in the problem list and clinic notes; he received warfarin during his June-2025 admission but current clinic medications (2026-08-04) are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only. Chart also documents congestive/acute systolic heart failure and essential hypertension, giving CHA2DS2-VASc 2, for which the 2023 AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. Needs review of whether anticoagulation should be restarted.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-listed and re-ordered at the 2026-08-20 clinic visit (current order a0184d35), together with aspirin and clopidogrel. The anticoagulant should not continue without prescriber review of the recent major bleed.

At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order c4b6df94) was re-ordered on the same day that apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7c496afb) was started, and the note's current-medication list contains both. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order should have been stopped.

Patient is on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list; current order e78404bf of 2026-07-12). His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 530 ms and Bazett QTc 539 ms, up from QTc 403 ms on the pre-amiodarone ECG of 2025-06-07. QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review per the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list; current order c67148bf of 2026-06-17) and warfarin. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 57 bpm with first-degree AV block, QT 556 ms and Bazett QTc 544 ms, which meets the clinic threshold of QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list medication and requires prescriber review. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17) are normal; no more recent ECG is on file.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm with an upright P wave before every QRS (PR 174 ms). QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -9 degrees (normal). QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 353 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66 bpm, PR 206 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 389 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new conduction block and the QTc change is less than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 132 ms, QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +49 degrees. Repolarisation is prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 484 ms, Bazett QTc 516 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2022-11-23 had QTc 354 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms; this is the tracing that was reviewed before escitalopram was started.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 160 ms, QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +44 degrees. The T wave is broad and late-peaking with QT 480 ms and Bazett QTc 519 ms, i.e. marked QT prolongation in a patient taking citalopram 40 mg daily. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2020-06-17 (regular tachycardia 132 bpm, QTc 404 ms) had a much shorter QTc, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees, QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with low-amplitude P waves preceding each QRS (PR approximately 120 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short-normal PR of about 110 ms. QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about -8 degrees (normal), QT 286 ms, Bazett QTc 364 ms. Tall R waves in V5 without bundle branch block. Only ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with PR 214 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS is broad at 122 ms with a QS/rS pattern in V1-V2 and a broad monophasic R wave in leads I and V6 - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -23 degrees. QT 434 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. The prior tracing of 2024-06-03 showed the same first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block with QTc 427 ms, so there is no interval change of 60 ms and no new conduction abnormality.

Atrial fibrillation: an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 102 bpm (RR intervals 0.39-1.07 s) with no organised P waves, only fibrillatory baseline undulation, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about -54 degrees (left axis deviation), QT 304 ms, Bazett QTc 396 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS (PR approximately 170 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, QT 430 ms, Bazett QTc 399 ms. Very tall R waves in V5-V6 (voltage criteria for LVH) but no bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57 bpm with ectopy, QTc 386 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 53 bpm (RR intervals 0.69-1.16 s). No P waves are discernible, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about +27 degrees, QT 412 ms, Bazett QTc 388 ms. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG three days earlier (2024-11-12) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves and PR 178 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with a small P wave before each QRS (PR approximately 130 ms). QRS has narrowed to 82 ms. Generalised low voltage with a predominantly negative QRS in leads I and aVF gives a frontal axis of about -175 degrees (extreme/right-superior axis). QT 282 ms, Bazett QTc 401 ms. The earlier tracing from the same admission (2024-12-05 01:33) showed a broad QRS of about 144 ms with a tall monophasic R in V1 and wide S in lead I (right bundle branch block); the conduction delay has resolved on this tracing. QTc changed from 458 to 401 ms, less than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 156 ms, narrow QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal), QT 382 ms with Bazett QTc 432 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2020-02-02 had a flat, prolonged repolarisation with QTc 502 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 70 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is recorded.

Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR 184 ms, QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about +69 degrees, QT 368 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The tracing is somewhat noisy in the limb leads but the rhythm is regular with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction. Only ECG on file.

Sinus bradycardia with sinus arrhythmia at about 58 bpm, prominent upright P waves in lead II, PR approximately 115 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +62 degrees, QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Deep S in V2 without bundle branch block. Compared with the prior tracing of the previous day (2025-03-08, sinus 62 bpm, QTc 422 ms) there is no meaningful change.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one early ectopic beat and a compensatory pause; P waves precede each conducted QRS with PR 200 ms (borderline first-degree AV block). QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about -31 degrees (left axis deviation, lead II net negative). QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 354 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about +44 degrees, QT 326 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior tracing of the previous day (2025-03-18, sinus 102 bpm, QTc 396 ms) there is no rhythm or conduction change and the QTc difference is less than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm with a low-amplitude P wave in lead II before each QRS (PR approximately 150 ms). QRS 96 ms, frontal axis about +33 degrees, QT 358 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 103 bpm with an upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 130 ms. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about +34 degrees, QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 373 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2025-06-20 showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with a rate-corrected QTc of about 473 ms; with the slower rate the QTc has fallen by roughly 100 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 applies.

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a low-amplitude P wave before each QRS (PR approximately 152 ms). QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal, borderline leftward; tall R in lead I with deep S in aVF). QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 435 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing of 2025-04-27 had a markedly different frontal-plane appearance (net negative lead I, axis about -173 degrees, suggesting limb-lead placement differences) with QTc 391 ms; there is no new atrial arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and the QTc change is less than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 144 ms, narrow QRS 66 ms, frontal axis about +50 degrees, QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 152 bpm (RR intervals 0.29-0.58 s). No organised P waves are present, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about -5 degrees, QT 252 ms, Bazett QTc 401 ms. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of the preceding evening (2025-09-12) showed a regular sinus rhythm at about 77 bpm with a single atrial premature beat, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, PR 158 ms, QRS 90 ms. The frontal axis is about -26 degrees (normal but leftward; tall R in lead I, predominantly negative QRS in aVF). QT 366 ms, Bazett QTc 383 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at about 120 bpm with a P wave preceding each QRS (PR approximately 165 ms; the P is partly merged with the preceding T at this rate). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +40 degrees, QT 272 ms and Bazett QTc 385 ms. No conduction block. Compared with the prior tracing of 2016-09-16 (sinus 108 bpm, QTc 391 ms) there is no significant change.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia, PR 170 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +7 degrees, QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 385 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block; this confirms the same-day clinic note describing sinus rhythm. The prior ECG of 2025-11-21 had a much longer repolarisation (QT 492 ms, QTc 521 ms), so the QTc has decreased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 174 ms, QRS 92 ms, frontal axis about +66 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad, late-peaking T wave best seen in V5: QT 530 ms, Bazett QTc 539 ms, in a patient started on amiodarone two weeks earlier. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm) had QT 454 ms with QTc 403 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 150 ms, narrow QRS 66 ms, frontal axis about +22 degrees, QT 364 ms, Bazett QTc 399 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file; it predates the escitalopram start of 2026-08-01, so it cannot serve as the post-start monitoring ECG.

Sinus rhythm at about 81 bpm with clear P waves in lead II and PR 184 ms; the rate varies gently with respiration. QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about +42 degrees, QT 326 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This confirms the same-day note describing sinus rhythm, and the QTc is normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. Only ECG on file.

Normal sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 146 ms, QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees, QT 354 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the surveillance tracing obtained after escitalopram was started and shows a normal QTc. Only ECG on file.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with a small atrial deflection before each QRS at a fixed PR of about 136 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 344 ms, Bazett QTc 370 ms. The QRS is deeply negative in leads I and II with a positive aVR, giving a frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis); precordial R-wave progression is preserved, so limb-lead reversal should be excluded clinically. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean rate of about 144 bpm (RR intervals 0.35-0.65 s) with a fibrillatory baseline and no discernible P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about +7 degrees, QT 286 ms, Bazett QTc 443 ms. No bundle branch block. The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 139 bpm with QTc 438 ms, so there is no interval change; this contradicts the clinic note of that day describing sinus rhythm at 72 bpm.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with PR 216 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about +11 degrees, QT 392 ms, Bazett QTc 373 ms. Tall R waves in V5 with deep S in V2 (voltage criteria for LVH) but no bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-30 showed sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR 186 ms and QTc 356 ms; the PR interval has lengthened but there is no new arrhythmia, no bundle branch block and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about +59 degrees, QT 316 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. Deep S waves in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6 but no bundle branch block. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day and is essentially identical (QTc 406 ms); no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 57 bpm with a consistent P wave before every QRS and PR 204 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms (no bundle branch block), frontal axis about +35 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: QT 556 ms, Bazett QTc 544 ms, in a patient on amiodarone. The prior ECG of 2022-04-06 showed atrial fibrillation at 131 bpm with QTc 437 ms, so sinus rhythm has been restored (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has risen by more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, PR 160 ms, narrow QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about +51 degrees, QT 292 ms with Bazett QTc 390 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2019-07-27 (sinus 75 bpm, QTc 413 ms) the rate is faster but there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm with a discrete atrial deflection preceding every QRS at a fixed interval of about 158 ms and an isoelectric baseline between atrial waves; best interpreted as sinus/atrial tachycardia rather than atrial fibrillation or flutter (the atrial and ventricular rates are 1:1). QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about -7 degrees, QT 290 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms. The prior tracing of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, no P waves) at 110 bpm, so organised atrial activity has been restored (RESOLVED_AF).

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, PR 194 ms (upper normal), QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about -27 degrees (still within the normal range), QT 334 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2021-05-16 (sinus 87 bpm, PR 144 ms, QTc 386 ms) the PR is longer and the axis more leftward, but there is no new arrhythmia, bundle branch block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms. Very deep S waves in V1-V3 with tall R in V5-V6 (voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy) but no bundle branch block. Essentially unchanged from the prior tracing of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QTc 384 ms).

QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about -7 degrees, QT 290 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms. The prior tracing of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, no P waves) at 110 bpm, so organised atrial activity has been restored (RESOLVED_AF).

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 160 ms, QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +44 degrees. The prior ECG of 2020-06-17 (regular tachycardia 132 bpm, QTc 404 ms) had a much shorter QTc, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees, QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with low-amplitude P waves preceding each QRS (PR approximately 120 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

The prior tracing of 2024-06-03 showed the same first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block with QTc 427 ms, so there is no interval change of 60 ms and no new conduction abnormality.

Atrial fibrillation: an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 102 bpm (RR intervals 0.39-1.07 s) with no organised P waves, only fibrillatory baseline undulation, so no measurable PR interval. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS (PR approximately 170 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, QT 430 ms, Bazett QTc 399 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57 bpm with ectopy, QTc 386 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 160 ms, QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +44 degrees. Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees, QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with low-amplitude P waves preceding each QRS (PR approximately 120 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short-normal PR of about 110 ms. QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about -8 degrees (normal), QT 286 ms, Bazett QTc 364 ms. Tall R waves in V5 without bundle branch block. Only ECG on file.

The prior tracing of 2024-06-03 showed the same first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block with QTc 427 ms, so there is no interval change of 60 ms and no new conduction abnormality.

Atrial fibrillation: an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 102 bpm (RR intervals 0.39-1.07 s) with no organised P waves, only fibrillatory baseline undulation, so no measurable PR interval. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS (PR approximately 170 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, QT 430 ms, Bazett QTc 399 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57 bpm with ectopy, QTc 386 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 53 bpm (RR intervals 0.69-1.16 s). No P waves are discernible, so the PR interval is not measurable. Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 160 ms, QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +44 degrees. The prior ECG of 2020-06-17 (regular tachycardia 132 bpm, QTc 404 ms) had a much shorter QTc, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees, QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with low-amplitude P waves preceding each QRS (PR approximately 120 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short-normal PR of about 110 ms. QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about -8 degrees (normal), QT 286 ms, Bazett QTc 364 ms. Tall R waves in V5 without bundle branch block. Only ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with PR 214 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS is broad at 122 ms with a QS/rS pattern in V1-V2 and a broad monophasic R wave in leads I and V6 - left bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 2024-06-03 showed the same first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block with QTc 427 ms, so there is no interval change of 60 ms and no new conduction abnormality.

Atrial fibrillation: an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 102 bpm (RR intervals 0.39-1.07 s) with no organised P waves, only fibrillatory baseline undulation, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about -54 degrees (left axis deviation), QT 304 ms, Bazett QTc 396 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS (PR approximately 170 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, QT 430 ms, Bazett QTc 399 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57 bpm with ectopy, QTc 386 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 53 bpm (RR intervals 0.69-1.16 s). No P waves are discernible, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about +27 degrees, QT 412 ms, Bazett QTc 388 ms. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG three days earlier (2024-11-12) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves and PR 178 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with a small P wave before each QRS (PR approximately 130 ms). QRS has narrowed to 82 ms. Generalised low voltage with a predominantly negative QRS in leads I and aVF gives a frontal axis of about -175 degrees (extreme/right-superior axis). QT 282 ms, Bazett QTc 401 ms. The earlier tracing from the same admission (2024-12-05 01:33) showed a broad QRS of about 144 ms with a tall monophasic R in V1 and wide S in lead I (right bundle branch block); the conduction delay has resolved on this tracing. QTc changed from 458 to 401 ms, less than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 156 ms, narrow QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal), QT 382 ms with Bazett QTc 432 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2020-02-02 had a flat, prolonged repolarisation with QTc 502 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 70 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is recorded.

Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR 184 ms, QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about +69 degrees, QT 368 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The tracing is somewhat noisy in the limb leads but the rhythm is regular with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction. Only ECG on file.

Sinus bradycardia with sinus arrhythmia at about 58 bpm, prominent upright P waves in lead II, PR approximately 115 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +62 degrees, QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one early ectopic beat and a compensatory pause; P waves precede each conducted QRS with PR 200 ms (borderline first-degree AV block). Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about +44 degrees, QT 326 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 144 ms, narrow QRS 66 ms, frontal axis about +50 degrees, QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

The prior ECG of the preceding evening (2025-09-12) showed a regular sinus rhythm at about 77 bpm with a single atrial premature beat, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

The prior tracing of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, no P waves) at 110 bpm, so organised atrial activity has been restored (RESOLVED_AF).

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, PR 194 ms (upper normal), QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about -27 degrees (still within the normal range), QT 334 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2021-05-16 (sinus 87 bpm, PR 144 ms, QTc 386 ms) the PR is longer and the axis more leftward, but there is no new arrhythmia, bundle branch block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms. Normal sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 156 ms, narrow QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal), QT 382 ms with Bazett QTc 432 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR 184 ms, QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about +69 degrees, QT 368 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The tracing is somewhat noisy in the limb leads but the rhythm is regular with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction. Only ECG on file.

Sinus bradycardia with sinus arrhythmia at about 58 bpm, prominent upright P waves in lead II, PR approximately 115 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +62 degrees, QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one early ectopic beat and a compensatory pause; P waves precede each conducted QRS with PR 200 ms (borderline first-degree AV block). Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about +44 degrees, QT 326 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm with a low-amplitude P wave in lead II before each QRS (PR approximately 150 ms). QRS 96 ms, frontal axis about +33 degrees, QT 358 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 144 ms, narrow QRS 66 ms, frontal axis about +50 degrees, QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 152 bpm (RR intervals 0.29-0.58 s). The prior ECG of the preceding evening (2025-09-12) showed a regular sinus rhythm at about 77 bpm with a single atrial premature beat, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Compared with the prior tracing of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66 bpm, PR 206 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 389 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new conduction block and the QTc change is less than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 132 ms, QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +49 degrees. Repolarisation is prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 484 ms, Bazett QTc 516 ms. Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 160 ms, QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +44 degrees. The prior ECG of 2020-06-17 (regular tachycardia 132 bpm, QTc 404 ms) had a much shorter QTc, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees, QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with low-amplitude P waves preceding each QRS (PR approximately 120 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short-normal PR of about 110 ms. QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about -8 degrees (normal), QT 286 ms, Bazett QTc 364 ms. Tall R waves in V5 without bundle branch block. Only ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with PR 214 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS is broad at 122 ms with a QS/rS pattern in V1-V2 and a broad monophasic R wave in leads I and V6 - left bundle branch block. Atrial fibrillation: an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 102 bpm (RR intervals 0.39-1.07 s) with no organised P waves, only fibrillatory baseline undulation, so no measurable PR interval. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS (PR approximately 170 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, QT 430 ms, Bazett QTc 399 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57 bpm with ectopy, QTc 386 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 53 bpm (RR intervals 0.69-1.16 s). No P waves are discernible, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about +27 degrees, QT 412 ms, Bazett QTc 388 ms. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG three days earlier (2024-11-12) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves and PR 178 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with a small P wave before each QRS (PR approximately 130 ms). QRS has narrowed to 82 ms. QTc changed from 458 to 401 ms, less than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 156 ms, narrow QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal), QT 382 ms with Bazett QTc 432 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR 184 ms, QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about +69 degrees, QT 368 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The tracing is somewhat noisy in the limb leads but the rhythm is regular with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction. Only ECG on file.

Sinus bradycardia with sinus arrhythmia at about 58 bpm, prominent upright P waves in lead II, PR approximately 115 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +62 degrees, QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one early ectopic beat and a compensatory pause; P waves precede each conducted QRS with PR 200 ms (borderline first-degree AV block). Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 144 ms, narrow QRS 66 ms, frontal axis about +50 degrees, QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 152 bpm (RR intervals 0.29-0.58 s). Sinus tachycardia at about 120 bpm with a P wave preceding each QRS (PR approximately 165 ms; the P is partly merged with the preceding T at this rate). Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia, PR 170 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +7 degrees, QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 385 ms. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm with a discrete atrial deflection preceding every QRS at a fixed interval of about 158 ms and an isoelectric baseline between atrial waves; best interpreted as sinus/atrial tachycardia rather than atrial fibrillation or flutter (the atrial and ventricular rates are 1:1). QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about -7 degrees, QT 290 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms. The prior tracing of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, no P waves) at 110 bpm, so organised atrial activity has been restored (RESOLVED_AF).

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, PR 194 ms (upper normal), QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about -27 degrees (still within the normal range), QT 334 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2021-05-16 (sinus 87 bpm, PR 144 ms, QTc 386 ms) the PR is longer and the axis more leftward, but there is no new arrhythmia, bundle branch block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms. Essentially unchanged from the prior tracing of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QTc 384 ms).

No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file.

items.explanation: Cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72." The note and the same-day ECGs conflict.

His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08 - the tracing that was reviewed when escitalopram was started) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 484 ms and Bazett QTc 516 ms, i.e. >= 500 ms, despite the 2024-05-14 note describing the QT as acceptable. Prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-03-18).

ECG 101538691 was obtained on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was completed; it showed sinus rhythm with QTc 378 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10. The start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. The only ECG on file (107859369) was not recorded until 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days (by 2026-08-15) under the revised memo. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so an ECG was due within 14 days (by 2026-08-24). That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15, so under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been recorded since the start (last tracing 2025-03-09), but the due date is after the 2026-09-24 review date, so the requirement is not yet due.

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler documents a warfarin dose increase from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily for a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, within the window, so the requirement was met.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-06-22) document persistent atrial fibrillation; she was also on a DOAC during a Jan-2025 admission (apixaban order a104f805). Current outpatient medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only - no oral anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age 80, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction with residual deficits, old myocardial infarction/coronary atherosclerosis, female). Guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is indicated; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD documents a warfarin dose decrease from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the anticoagulation protocol for a home INR of 3.4 (a dose change a clinic pharmacist is permitted to make). The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since 2026-06-17, so the follow-up INR is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (Condition 7010d0e5) carried in every cardiology clinic note. Current medications at the last visit (2026-06-27) are levothyroxine only - no anticoagulant and no record of one being stopped for a documented reason. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition 66dd1300) and prior embolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis. Current medications at the last clinic visit (2026-06-23) are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate - no anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke, female). Anticoagulation is strongly indicated for secondary stroke prevention.

48-year-old man with atrial fibrillation/paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in the problem list and clinic notes; he received warfarin during his June-2025 admission but current clinic medications (2026-08-04) are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only. Chart also documents congestive/acute systolic heart failure and essential hypertension, giving CHA2DS2-VASc 2, for which the 2023 AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. Needs review of whether anticoagulation should be restarted.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2/2026-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-listed and re-ordered at the 2026-08-20 clinic visit (current order a0184d35), together with aspirin and clopidogrel. The anticoagulant should not continue without prescriber review of the recent major bleed.

At the 2026-07-15 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order c4b6df94) was re-ordered on the same day that apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7c496afb) was started, and the note's current-medication list contains both. Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order should have been stopped.

QTc >= 500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review per the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal.

QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 353 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 2018-12-13 (sinus 66 bpm, PR 206 ms, QRS 100 ms, QTc 389 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new conduction block and the QTc change is less than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 132 ms, QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +49 degrees. Repolarisation is prolonged with a broad low-amplitude T wave: QT 484 ms, Bazett QTc 516 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2022-11-23 had QTc 354 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms; this is the tracing that was reviewed before escitalopram was started.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 160 ms, QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +44 degrees. The T wave is broad and late-peaking with QT 480 ms and Bazett QTc 519 ms, i.e. marked QT prolongation in a patient taking citalopram 40 mg daily. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2020-06-17 (regular tachycardia 132 bpm, QTc 404 ms) had a much shorter QTc, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, PR 136 ms, narrow QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees, QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with low-amplitude P waves preceding each QRS (PR approximately 120 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS and a short-normal PR of about 110 ms. QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about -8 degrees (normal), QT 286 ms, Bazett QTc 364 ms. Tall R waves in V5 without bundle branch block. Only ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with PR 214 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS is broad at 122 ms with a QS/rS pattern in V1-V2 and a broad monophasic R wave in leads I and V6 - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -23 degrees. QT 434 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. The prior tracing of 2024-06-03 showed the same first-degree AV block and left bundle branch block with QTc 427 ms, so there is no interval change of 60 ms and no new conduction abnormality.

Atrial fibrillation: an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 102 bpm (RR intervals 0.39-1.07 s) with no organised P waves, only fibrillatory baseline undulation, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about -54 degrees (left axis deviation), QT 304 ms, Bazett QTc 396 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS (PR approximately 170 ms). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, QT 430 ms, Bazett QTc 399 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57 bpm with ectopy, QTc 386 ms) there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 53 bpm (RR intervals 0.69-1.16 s). No P waves are discernible, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about +27 degrees, QT 412 ms, Bazett QTc 388 ms. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG three days earlier (2024-11-12) showed regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves and PR 178 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with a small P wave before each QRS (PR approximately 130 ms). QRS has narrowed to 82 ms. Generalised low voltage with a predominantly negative QRS in leads I and aVF gives a frontal axis of about -175 degrees (extreme/right-superior axis). QT 282 ms, Bazett QTc 401 ms. The earlier tracing from the same admission (2024-12-05 01:33) showed a broad QRS of about 144 ms with a tall monophasic R in V1 and wide S in lead I (right bundle branch block); the conduction delay has resolved on this tracing. QTc changed from 458 to 401 ms, less than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 156 ms, narrow QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal), QT 382 ms with Bazett QTc 432 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2020-02-02 had a flat, prolonged repolarisation with QTc 502 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 70 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is recorded.

Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, PR 184 ms, QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about +69 degrees, QT 368 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The tracing is somewhat noisy in the limb leads but the rhythm is regular with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction. Only ECG on file.

Sinus bradycardia with sinus arrhythmia at about 58 bpm, prominent upright P waves in lead II, PR approximately 115 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +62 degrees, QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Deep S in V2 without bundle branch block. Compared with the prior tracing of the previous day (2025-03-08, sinus 62 bpm, QTc 422 ms) there is no meaningful change.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one early ectopic beat and a compensatory pause; P waves precede each conducted QRS with PR 200 ms (borderline first-degree AV block). QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about -31 degrees (left axis deviation, lead II net negative). QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 354 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about +44 degrees, QT 326 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior tracing of the previous day (2025-03-18, sinus 102 bpm, QTc 396 ms) there is no rhythm or conduction change and the QTc difference is less than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm with a low-amplitude P wave in lead II before each QRS (PR approximately 150 ms). QRS 96 ms, frontal axis about +33 degrees, QT 358 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 103 bpm with an upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 130 ms. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about +34 degrees, QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 373 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2025-06-20 showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with a rate-corrected QTc of about 473 ms; with the slower rate the QTc has fallen by roughly 100 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 applies.

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a low-amplitude P wave before each QRS (PR approximately 152 ms). The prior tracing of 2025-04-27 had a markedly different frontal-plane appearance (net negative lead I, axis about -173 degrees, suggesting limb-lead placement differences) with QTc 391 ms; there is no new atrial arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and the QTc change is less than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, PR 144 ms, narrow QRS 66 ms, frontal axis about +50 degrees, QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 152 bpm (RR intervals 0.29-0.58 s). No organised P waves are present, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about -5 degrees, QT 252 ms, Bazett QTc 401 ms. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of the preceding evening (2025-09-12) showed a regular sinus rhythm at about 77 bpm with a single atrial premature beat, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, PR 158 ms, QRS 90 ms. The frontal axis is about -26 degrees (normal but leftward; tall R in lead I, predominantly negative QRS in aVF). QT 366 ms, Bazett QTc 383 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at about 120 bpm with a P wave preceding each QRS (PR approximately 165 ms; the P is partly merged with the preceding T at this rate). QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +40 degrees, QT 272 ms and Bazett QTc 385 ms. No conduction block. Compared with the prior tracing of 2016-09-16 (sinus 108 bpm, QTc 391 ms) there is no significant change.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia, PR 170 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +7 degrees, QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 385 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block; this confirms the same-day clinic note describing sinus rhythm. The prior ECG of 2025-11-21 had a much longer repolarisation (QT 492 ms, QTc 521 ms), so the QTc has decreased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 174 ms, QRS 92 ms, frontal axis about +66 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad, late-peaking T wave best seen in V5: QT 530 ms, Bazett QTc 539 ms, in a patient started on amiodarone two weeks earlier. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm) had QT 454 ms with QTc 403 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 150 ms, narrow QRS 66 ms, frontal axis about +22 degrees, QT 364 ms, Bazett QTc 399 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file; it predates the escitalopram start of 2026-08-01, so it cannot serve as the post-start monitoring ECG.

Sinus rhythm at about 81 bpm with clear P waves in lead II and PR 184 ms; the rate varies gently with respiration. QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about +42 degrees, QT 326 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This confirms the same-day note describing sinus rhythm, and the QTc is normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. Only ECG on file.

Normal sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 146 ms, QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees, QT 354 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the surveillance tracing obtained after escitalopram was started and shows a normal QTc. Only ECG on file.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with a small atrial deflection before each QRS at a fixed PR of about 136 ms. QRS 86 ms, QT 344 ms, Bazett QTc 370 ms. The QRS is deeply negative in leads I and II with a positive aVR, giving a frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis); precordial R-wave progression is preserved, so limb-lead reversal should be excluded clinically. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean rate of about 144 bpm (RR intervals 0.35-0.65 s) with a fibrillatory baseline and no discernible P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about +7 degrees, QT 286 ms, Bazett QTc 443 ms. No bundle branch block. The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 139 bpm with QTc 438 ms, so there is no interval change; this contradicts the clinic note of that day describing sinus rhythm at 72 bpm.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about +59 degrees, QT 316 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. Deep S waves in V1-V2 with tall R in V5-V6 but no bundle branch block. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day and is essentially identical (QTc 406 ms); no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 57 bpm with a consistent P wave before every QRS and PR 204 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms (no bundle branch block), frontal axis about +35 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: QT 556 ms, Bazett QTc 544 ms, in a patient on amiodarone. The prior ECG of 2022-04-06 showed atrial fibrillation at 131 bpm with QTc 437 ms, so sinus rhythm has been restored (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has risen by more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, PR 160 ms, narrow QRS 64 ms, frontal axis about +51 degrees, QT 292 ms with Bazett QTc 390 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2019-07-27 (sinus 75 bpm, QTc 413 ms) the rate is faster but there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm with a discrete atrial deflection preceding every QRS at a fixed interval of about 158 ms and an isoelectric baseline between atrial waves; best interpreted as sinus/atrial tachycardia rather than atrial fibrillation or flutter (the atrial and ventricular rates are 1:1). QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about -7 degrees, QT 290 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms. The prior tracing of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, no P waves) at 110 bpm, so organised atrial activity has been restored (RESOLVED_AF).

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, PR 194 ms (upper normal), QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about -27 degrees (still within the normal range), QT 334 ms, Bazett QTc 411 ms. No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2021-05-16 (sinus 87 bpm, PR 144 ms, QTc 386 ms) the PR is longer and the axis more leftward, but there is no new arrhythmia, bundle branch block or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees, QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms. Very deep S waves in V1-V3 with tall R in V5-V6 (voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy) but no bundle branch block. Essentially unchanged from the prior tracing of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QTc 384 ms).

CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age 80, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction with residual deficits, old myocardial infarction/coronary atherosclerosis, female). Guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is indicated; aspirin is not an adequate substitute.

Nguyen, PharmD documents a warfarin dose decrease from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the anticoagulation protocol for a home INR of 3.4 (a dose change a clinic pharmacist is permitted to make). The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since 2026-06-17, so the follow-up INR is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended.

Anticoagulation is strongly indicated for secondary stroke prevention.

Needs review of whether anticoagulation should be restarted.

The anticoagulant should not continue without prescriber review of the recent major bleed.

Two concurrent oral anticoagulants create a major bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order should have been stopped.
